{{Short description|Neighborhood of Newark, New Jersey, US}} {{Use American English|date=July 2023}} {{Use mdy dates|date=July 2023}} [[File:St. Stephan's Church - Ironbound, Newark.jpg|thumb|250px|[[St. Stephan's Church (Ironbound, Newark, New Jersey)|St. Stephan's Church]] is an Ironbound landmark, built in 1874.]] [[File:Ironbound Views.jpg|alt=|thumb|Ironbound Views of the Newark Skyline]] The '''Ironbound'''{{efn|Often referred to with a [[wiktionary:definite article|definite article]], e.g., '''The Ironbound.'''}} is a neighborhood in the city of [[Newark, New Jersey|Newark]] in [[Essex County, New Jersey|Essex County]], in the [[U.S. state]] of [[New Jersey]].{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/03/01/realestate/the-ironbound-newark-convenient-but-a-world-apart.html|title=The Ironbound, Newark: Convenient, but a World Apart|first=Julie|last=Lasky|newspaper=The New York Times|date=1 March 2017|access-date=11 February 2018}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052748703886904576031681807027592|title=A Multicultural River Bend|newspaper=Wall Street Journal|date=31 December 2010|last1=Sussman|first1=Anna Louie|archive-date=July 20, 2019|access-date=July 20, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190720054246/https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052748703886904576031681807027592|url-status=live}} It is a large working-class multi-ethnic community, covering about {{convert|4|sqmi|sqkm}}. Historically, the area was called "'''Dutch Neck'''", "'''Down Neck'''", or simply "'''the Neck'''", for its location by a bend of the [[Passaic River]].Lawlor, Julia. [https://www.nytimes.com/2004/01/11/realestate/11LIVI.html "If You're Thinking of Living In/The Ironbound; A Home Away From Home for Immigrants"], ''[[The New York Times]]'', January 11, 2004. Accessed June 26, 2013. Part of Newark's East Ward, the Ironbound is directly east of [[Pennsylvania Station (Newark)|Newark Penn Station]] and [[Downtown Newark]], and south and west of the river. The neighborhood is connected by the [[Jackson Street Bridge]] over the river to [[Harrison, New Jersey|Harrison]] and [[Kearny, New Jersey|Kearny]].The area became a major transmission "hotspot" of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in New Jersey|COVID-19 pandemic]] in late 2020. {{cite news|date=November 20, 2020|title=Newark mayor asks all city residents to shelter in place for 10 days after Thanksgiving|work=News12 The Bronx|url=https://bronx.news12.com/newark-mayor-asks-all-city-residents-to-shelter-in-place-for-days-after-thanksgiving|access-date=21 November 2020|quote=There are also mandatory curfews in place for hot zones, like the Ironbound section of the city...|archive-date=November 26, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201126034610/https://bronx.news12.com/newark-mayor-asks-all-city-residents-to-shelter-in-place-for-days-after-thanksgiving|url-status=live}}{{cite news|last1=Sutton|first1=Sam|date=October 26, 2020|title='It's a desperate moment': Newark mayor imposes new Covid restrictions as cases surge|work=[[Politico]]|url=https://www.politico.com/states/new-jersey/story/2020/10/26/its-a-desperate-moment-newark-mayor-imposes-new-covid-restrictions-as-cases-surge-1330820|access-date=21 November 2020|quote=...recent spikes are even more dramatic in the Ironbound section of Newark’s East Ward...|archive-date=November 26, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201126135432/https://www.politico.com/states/new-jersey/story/2020/10/26/its-a-desperate-moment-newark-mayor-imposes-new-covid-restrictions-as-cases-surge-1330820|url-status=live}} ==Early history== [[File:1910-era ethnic map of Newark, New Jersey.jpg|thumb|1910-era map of ethnic enclaves in [[Newark, New Jersey]]]]The area was mostly farmland until the 1830s, when industry and immigration began increasing at a rapid pace.{{Cite web |last=impressM |title=The Ironbound's Early History. Part I: Immigrants, Industry Remake a Once-Bucolic Down Neck |url=https://knowingnewark.npl.org/the-ironbounds-early-history-part-i-immigrants-industry-remake-a-once-bucolic-down-neck/ |access-date=2021-12-29 |website=Charles Cummings |archive-date=December 29, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211229011501/https://knowingnewark.npl.org/the-ironbounds-early-history-part-i-immigrants-industry-remake-a-once-bucolic-down-neck/ |url-status=live }} The name "The Ironbound" is said to derive from the large metalworking industry in the area or from the network of railroad tracks that surrounded the neighborhood. === Industry === The Ironbound was an industrial neighborhood in the 19th and early 20th centuries. The neighborhood was home to Hensler's Beer Brewery, [[P. Ballantine and Sons Brewing Company|P. Ballantine and Sons Brewing Company (in 1954 Newark's largest employer)]] and the [[Christian William Feigenspan|Feigenspan Brewery]].{{Cite web|last=impressM|title=In a Glass Darkly: Beer Marks City's History Brewers Benefited from Workers, Water|url=https://knowingnewark.npl.org/in-a-glass-darkly-beer-marks-citys-history-brewers-benefited-from-workers-water/|access-date=2021-12-29|website=Charles Cummings|archive-date=December 29, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211229011502/https://knowingnewark.npl.org/in-a-glass-darkly-beer-marks-citys-history-brewers-benefited-from-workers-water/|url-status=live}} [[Balbach Smelting & Refining Company]], now the location of [[Riverbank Park]], was the second largest metal processing enterprise in the United States until its closure in the 1920s.{{cite web|author=J. Bennett|title=Riverbank Park in Newark|url=http://www.newarkhistory.com/riverbank.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925004808/http://www.newarkhistory.com/riverbank.html|archive-date=September 25, 2015|access-date=October 29, 2015|work=Newarkology}} Other large industrial buildings included [[Murphy Varnish Works]].{{Cite web|last=impressM|title=The Ironbound. Part II: Industry, Commerce Sustain Vibrant Soul in Midst of Change|url=https://knowingnewark.npl.org/the-ironbound-part-ii-industry-commerce-sustain-vibrant-soul-in-midst-of-change/|access-date=2021-12-29|website=Charles Cummings|archive-date=December 29, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211229011506/https://knowingnewark.npl.org/the-ironbound-part-ii-industry-commerce-sustain-vibrant-soul-in-midst-of-change/|url-status=live}} === Immigration === The Ironbound has experienced several waves of immigration. The first wave, starting in the 1830s, came from the German states. Wrote historian Charles Cummings, "Overnight, whole sections of the Ironbound became Irish and German". Polish and Italian immigrants arrived in the latter half of the 19th century, followed by Portuguese and Spanish starting in the 1910s.{{Cite web|last=impressM|title=Rich Spanish Influence Runs Deep in City|url=https://knowingnewark.npl.org/rich-spanish-influence-runs-deep-in-city/|access-date=2021-12-14|website=Charles Cummings|archive-date=December 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211214164755/https://knowingnewark.npl.org/rich-spanish-influence-runs-deep-in-city/|url-status=live}} By 1921 there was a large enough Portuguese population to found Sport Club Portuguese,{{Cite web|title=Sport Club Português Celebrates 100 years Through Art and Culture Exhibit|url=https://www.tapinto.net/towns/newark/sections/arts-and-entertainment/articles/sport-club-portugues-celebrates-100-years-through-art-and-culture-exhibit|access-date=2021-12-14|website=TAPinto|language=en|archive-date=December 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211214164801/https://www.tapinto.net/towns/newark/sections/arts-and-entertainment/articles/sport-club-portugues-celebrates-100-years-through-art-and-culture-exhibit|url-status=live}} the first of over twenty Portuguese social clubs that would call the Ironbound home.{{Cite news|last=Lawlor|first=Julia|date=2004-01-11|title=If You're Thinking of Living In/The Ironbound; A Home Away From Home for Immigrants|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/01/11/realestate/if-you-re-thinking-living-ironbound-home-away-home-for-immigrants.html|access-date=2021-12-14|issn=0362-4331|archive-date=December 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211214164753/https://www.nytimes.com/2004/01/11/realestate/if-you-re-thinking-living-ironbound-home-away-home-for-immigrants.html|url-status=live}}[[Image:Firehouse 8 Filmore jeh.JPG|thumb|Former Firehouse 8 on Ferry Street]] === Historical landmarks === The following sites in the Ironbound are on the [[National Register of Historic Places]]: * [[Murphy Varnish Works]] * [[Pennsylvania Station (Newark)]] * [[Riverbank Park]] * [[St. Casimir's Roman Catholic Church (Newark, New Jersey)]] * [[St. Stephan's Church (Ironbound, Newark, New Jersey)]] ==Culture and commerce== Ferry Street is the main commercial strip in the area. In 2017,{{Cite news |last=Lasky |first=Julie |date=2017-03-01 |title=The Ironbound, Newark: Convenient, but a World Apart |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/03/01/realestate/the-ironbound-newark-convenient-but-a-world-apart.html |access-date=2023-02-16 |issn=0362-4331}} the ''New York Times'' described the neighborhood as:
Four square miles populated in large part by Portuguese, Spanish and Latin American immigrants and their descendants, the Ironbound has the intimacy and hustle of a European market town. “We walk to the bakery, the fishmonger, the wine store,” said [the director of the [[Newark Museum of Art]]]. (He also walks to work.) “It really is an extraordinarily agreeable lifestyle.”
===Portuguese community=== The Ironbound is known for being a [[Portuguese-American|Portuguese]] neighborhood.Shepard, Richard F. [https://www.nytimes.com/1982/03/26/arts/exploring-cultural-pleasures-newark-april-portugal-waiting-just-across-hudson.html "EXPLORING THE CULTURAL PLEASURES OF NEWARK - April in Portugal is Waiting Just Across the Hudson"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160807113342/http://www.nytimes.com/1982/03/26/arts/exploring-cultural-pleasures-newark-april-portugal-waiting-just-across-hudson.html |date=August 7, 2016 }}, ''[[The New York Times]]'', March 26, 1982. Accessed June 26, 2013. [[TAP Air Portugal]] has its corporate office in the neighborhood. Ironbound Volunteer Ambulance Squad has been serving the community since 1952.{{Cite web|title=Ironbound Ambulance Squad {{!}} Newark, NJ|url=http://www.ironboundambulance.org/|access-date=2021-12-14|website=www.ironboundambulance.org|archive-date=December 9, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211209035258/http://ironboundambulance.org/|url-status=live}} Ironbound also has its own newspaper. Many Portuguese still live in the Ironbound, but many are moving out to other neighborhoods in New Jersey, Including [[South River, New Jersey|South River]], [[Livingston, New Jersey|Livingston]], [[Clark, New Jersey|Clark]], [[Westfield, New Jersey|Westfield]], [[Watchung, New Jersey|Watchung]], [[Old Bridge Township, New Jersey|Old Bridge]], etc. ====Peter Francisco Park==== A small sitting park east of Penn Station is named in honor of [[Peter Francisco]], a Portuguese-born patriot of the American War of Independence. An obelisk in Francisco's memory was raised in the park by the Portuguese community in 1976. [[Peter Francisco Park]] also features a memorial to Portuguese-American war veterans dedicated in 2018 as well as the Ironbound Immigrants Memorial, dedicated in 2019. ==Festivals== ===Portugal Day festival=== The neighborhood holds the annual [[Portugal Day Festival in Newark|Portuguese Parade & Festival]], known as Portugal Day, in early June{{Cite news|last=Kurtz|first=Gretchen|date=2001-05-20|title=Summer in the City. Yes, That City.|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2001/05/20/nyregion/summer-in-the-city-yes-that-city.html|access-date=2021-12-14|issn=0362-4331|archive-date=December 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211214195837/https://www.nytimes.com/2001/05/20/nyregion/summer-in-the-city-yes-that-city.html|url-status=live}} During [[Portugal Day Festival in Newark|Portugal Day]] Weekend, many people come out to celebrate Portuguese-American culture. Ferry Street is also the location for most soccer fans to come and celebrate.{{Citation|title=Portugal Brazil world cup celebration newark nj pt4|date=June 25, 2010|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eupXVnypS_g|language=en|access-date=2021-12-14|archive-date=December 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211214195837/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eupXVnypS_g&gl=US&hl=en|url-status=live}}{{Citation|title=Portugal Ferry St. Celebration after Czech win|date=June 22, 2012|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1TMWPayffzw|language=en|access-date=2021-12-14|archive-date=December 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211214195836/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1TMWPayffzw|url-status=live}}{{Citation|title=Spain Wins vs Germany Ironbound Newark NJ Ferry Street|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LHQ_vhB1R5c|language=en|access-date=2021-12-14|archive-date=December 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211214195837/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LHQ_vhB1R5c|url-status=live}}{{Citation|title=EURO 2016: Portugal defeats France to win EURO! Fans celebrate in Newark, NJ. (July 10, 2016).| date=May 21, 2017 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4mo2s3I_lDM|language=en|access-date=2021-12-14}} Fans walk up and down the street while others decorate their cars and celebrate the victory of their soccer team. === Ecuadorian Day festival === Typically held in the first or second weekend of August, the Ecuadorian Day Parade & festival take place in Ferry Street.{{Cite web|title=The Annual Ecuadorian Festival And Parade Of Newark {{!}} Inca Kola|url=https://incakolausa.com/the-annual-ecuadorian-festival-and-parade-of-newark/|access-date=2021-12-14|website=incakolausa.com|archive-date=December 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211214195839/https://incakolausa.com/the-annual-ecuadorian-festival-and-parade-of-newark/|url-status=live}} In this event various businesses and politicians attend the parade and support the Ecuadorian culture in a statewide recognized festivity. === Brazilian Day festival === Typically held in the first or second weekend of September, the Brazilian day festival takes place also in Ferry Street.{{Cite web|title=Newark Brazilian Day {{!}} Discover Events, Parades & Festivals|url=https://www.newarkhappening.com/brazilian-day/|access-date=2021-12-14|website=www.newarkhappening.com|language=en-us|archive-date=December 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211214195838/https://www.newarkhappening.com/brazilian-day/|url-status=live}} Various street vendors, musical concerts, and restaurants show support for Brazilian culture. ===Italian festival=== [[Our Lady of Mt. Carmel]], the Ironbound's first Italian parish, holds an annual Italian festival.{{Cite web|url=http://www.newarkhistory.com/independencepark.html|title=Independence Park|access-date=May 5, 2018|archive-date=June 25, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180625024932/http://www.newarkhistory.com/independencepark.html|url-status=live}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/OLMCNEWARK|title=Our Lady of Mount Carmel Church - Newark, NJ|website=www.facebook.com|access-date=May 5, 2018|archive-date=April 9, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200409202434/https://www.facebook.com/OLMCNEWARK/|url-status=live}} ==Demographics== [[File:IronboundImmigrantsMemorialNewark.png|thumb|The Ironbound Immigrants Memorial (2018) in [[Peter Francisco Park]] in the westernmost area the Ironbound section outside [[Newark Penn Station]].]] The Ironbound used to mainly consist of [[Italian Americans|Italians]], [[Polish Americans|Polish]], [[Portuguese Americans|Portuguese]], and [[Spaniard American|Spaniard]] Immigrants. As time went on many Italian and Polish immigrants have moved out of the Ironbound. However, there are still significant numbers of residents of Italian and Polish descent residing in the Ironbound. Recent immigrants include large numbers of Brazilians and Ecuadorians.{{Cite web|title=Explore Census Data|url=https://data.census.gov/cedsci/|access-date=2021-12-29|website=data.census.gov|archive-date=May 5, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210505140923/https://data.census.gov/cedsci/|url-status=live}}{{Cite web|title=Little Portugal in Newark|url=http://bkpk.me/little-portugal-in-newark/|access-date=2021-12-29|website=bkpk.me|language=en-US}} 2000s census demographics include: 57.46% White/Caucasian/European (Mainly consisting of [[Italians|Italian]], [[Spaniards|Spanish]], [[Polish Americans|Polish]], and other European Ethnicity) 34.94% Hispanic & Latino (Mainly consisting of [[Ecuadorian Americans|Ecuadorians]], Etc.) 0.95% Asian/American Indian 4.68% Black/African American 1.97% Multi-Racial ==Parks and recreation== ===Independence Park=== This park is in the Ironbound district.{{Cite web|url=https://www.essexcountyparks.org/parks/independence-park|title=Independence Park | Parks | Essex County Parks|access-date=May 5, 2018|archive-date=April 23, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180423232512/https://www.essexcountyparks.org/parks/independence-park|url-status=live}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.google.com/maps/place/Independence+Park/@40.7242486,-74.1629214,16.71z/data=!4m8!1m2!2m1!1snewark+nj!3m4!1s0x89c25399c1b34447:0xd09dd6610df3e459!8m2!3d40.7243845!4d-74.1604963|title = Google Maps}} [[Our Lady of Mt. Carmel]], the Ironbound's first Italian parish, faces the park. The church holds an annual Italian festival which attracts Italian-American people that live in the neighborhood, and Italians who moved out of the Ironbound. ===Riverfront Park and waterfront=== [[File:RiverbankParkOrangeBoardwalkNewark1.tiff|thumb|Orange Boardwalk and [[Jackson Street Bridge]]]] A chain of parkland along the [[Passaic River]], especially along the downward "curve" in the river that gave the [[Ironbound]] neighborhood its nickname of "Down Neck," offers waterfront recreation in the city. *[[Peter Francisco Park]] is a small park near Penn Station in honor of the Portuguese-born Revolution-era patriot. ==Education== ===Public schools=== The [[Newark Public Schools]] operates six elementary and K-8 schools in the area. Schools serving Ironbound include Wilson Avenue School, Hawkins Street School, Lafayette Street School and Oliver Street School. In addition is Ann Street School, which is considered by many to be one of the best elementary schools in the city and the K-5 South Street School. In fact, Ann Street School received the Blue Ribbon School of Excellence from the US Department of Education. This competitive award had not been awarded to a Newark Public School before. In addition, the award prompted then Vice President of the US, Al Gore, to visit Ann Street to promote the importance of the upcoming 2000 US Census.Erminio, Vanessa. [http://www.nj.com/newark/index.ssf/2007/11/neighborhood_snapshot_ironboun.html "Neighborhood snapshot: Ironbound"], ''[[The Star-Ledger]]''. November 8, 2007. Accessed June 26, 2013."[http://www.nps.k12.nj.us/schools.html Newark Public Schools 2008-2009 Directory] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101104201427/http://www.nps.k12.nj.us/schools.html |date=2010-11-04 }}." [[Newark Public Schools]]. Retrieved on March 2, 2010. [[East Side High School (Newark, New Jersey)|East Side High School]] serves Ironbound high school students. As of 2004 most of the elementary schools were built over 100 years prior to the time. In the 2000s, an increase in housing lead to an overcrowding of Ironbound-area schools. At the time the school district planned to replace several of the elementary schools and build a new East Side High School in the former Ballantine brewery site. ===Private schools=== The [[Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Newark]] operates the Ironbound Catholic Academy, a PK-8 school in Ironbound."[http://mysite.verizon.net/stcas/id6.html St. Casimir Academy] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110606013640/http://mysite.verizon.net/stcas/id6.html |date=June 6, 2011 }}." St. Casimir Roman Catholic Church. Retrieved on March 2, 2010. "The mission of the Christian Community of St. Casimir Academy(Pre-Kindergarten through Grade 8), calls us to serve the children within the Ironbound area of the Newark Archdiocese by providing them with a total education based on the teachings of Jesus, through which Christian principals and moral values become a part of each students character and life.""[http://www.rcan.org/schools/essex.html Essex County Catholic Elementary Schools] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100214072441/http://www.rcan.org/SCHOOLS/essex.html |date=2010-02-14 }}." [[Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Newark]]. Retrieved on March 2, 2010. As of 2004 many residents of Ironbound send their children to parochial schools. Ironbound used to have three other Catholic elementary schools, including Academy of St. Benedict, a PreK-8 school, St. James, both elementary and high school, and St. Lucy Filippini Academy.[https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=940CE2DE103DF930A35750C0A9639C8B63 "New Jersey: Newark: Seven Catholic Schools To Close"], ''[[The New York Times]]''. March 3, 2005. Retrieved on March 2, 2010. In 2005 the archdiocese announced that St. Casimir, St. Benedict, and St. Lucy Filippini would merge into the Ironbound Catholic Academy on the St. Casimir site. There is also the Our Lady of Fatima Nursery, a Pre-K institution and one Portuguese Language School known at Escola Luis de Camões. ===Public libraries=== [[Newark Public Library]]'s Van Buren Branch Library serves the Ironbound neighborhood. The library opened on September 23, 1923. A renovated and expanded branch opened on November 19, 1997.[http://www.npl.org/Pages/Branches/VanBuren/VanBuren.html Van Buren Branch Library], [[Newark Public Library]]. Retrieved on March 2, 2010. == Housing == About 60% of the real estate market in the Ironbound is two- and three-family houses.{{Cite news|last=Lawlor|first=Julia|date=2004-01-11|title=If You're Thinking of Living In/The Ironbound; A Home Away From Home for Immigrants|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/01/11/realestate/if-you-re-thinking-living-ironbound-home-away-home-for-immigrants.html|access-date=2021-12-28|issn=0362-4331|archive-date=December 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211214164753/https://www.nytimes.com/2004/01/11/realestate/if-you-re-thinking-living-ironbound-home-away-home-for-immigrants.html|url-status=live}} Many houses built by the Portuguese include tile details and aluminum siding.{{Cite news|last=Ferretti|first=Fred|date=1978-03-12|title=ABOUT NEW JERSEY|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1978/03/12/archives/new-jersey-weekly-about-new-jersey-a-pictorial-record-of-newarks.html|access-date=2021-12-28|issn=0362-4331|archive-date=December 28, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211228223534/https://www.nytimes.com/1978/03/12/archives/new-jersey-weekly-about-new-jersey-a-pictorial-record-of-newarks.html|url-status=live}} In the past ten to fifteen years, more luxury condos and apartments have been built in the area.{{Cite web|last=Star-Ledger|first=Carmen Juri/The|date=2008-07-16|title=Luxury condos coming to Newark|url=https://www.nj.com/newark/2008/07/luxury_condos_coming_to_newark.html|access-date=2021-12-28|website=nj|language=en|archive-date=December 28, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211228223530/https://www.nj.com/newark/2008/07/luxury_condos_coming_to_newark.html|url-status=live}} Several old factory buildings have been converted into lofts or apartments including Textile Lofts,{{Cite web|title=Official Site {{!}} Textile Lofts Apartments - Newark NJ|url=https://www.textileloftsnewark.com/|access-date=2021-12-28|website=Textile Lofts|language=en|archive-date=December 28, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211228223536/https://www.textileloftsnewark.com/|url-status=live}} Button Factory Lofts,{{Cite web|title=Button Factory Lofts Apartments - Newark, NJ|url=https://www.apartments.com/button-factory-lofts-newark-nj/b44pze8/|access-date=2021-12-28|website=Apartments.com|language=en|archive-date=December 13, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241213224608/https://www.apartments.com/button-factory-lofts-newark-nj/b44pze8/|url-status=live}} Murphy Varnish Factory,{{Cite web|last=NJ.com|first=Barry Carter {{!}} NJ Advance Media for|date=2019-06-16|title=It went from factory to contaminated mess. Now it's restored and renting apartments.|url=https://www.nj.com/essex/2019/06/it-went-from-historic-factory-to-contaminated-mess-now-its-restored-and-renting-apartments.html|access-date=2021-12-28|website=nj|language=en|archive-date=December 28, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211228223529/https://www.nj.com/essex/2019/06/it-went-from-historic-factory-to-contaminated-mess-now-its-restored-and-renting-apartments.html|url-status=live}} and the Chocolate Factory.{{Cite web|title=109 Hamilton St, Newark, NJ 07105 - Condo for Rent in Newark, NJ|url=https://www.apartments.com/109-hamilton-st-newark-nj/h7wf9m1/|access-date=2021-12-28|website=Apartments.com|language=en|archive-date=December 17, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241217143240/https://www.apartments.com/109-hamilton-st-newark-nj/h7wf9m1/|url-status=live}} Ironbound has three housing projects within its boundaries: Hyatt Court, Pennington Court, and Terrell Homes (formerly Franklin Delano Roosevelt Homes).{{Cite web|last=impressM|title=Three Powerful Agencies Brought Housing to the City's Needy|url=https://knowingnewark.npl.org/three-powerful-agencies-brought-housing-to-the-citys-needy/|access-date=2021-12-28|website=Charles Cummings|archive-date=December 28, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211228223535/https://knowingnewark.npl.org/three-powerful-agencies-brought-housing-to-the-citys-needy/|url-status=live}} Tenants and activists have recently been in a battle with the Newark Housing Authority to save Terrell Homes, which the Authority had planned to demolish. == Environmental justice == The Ironbound has a "national reputation"{{Cite web|title=Project Showcase: Ironbound Environmental Justice History and Resource Center {{!}} National Council on Public History|url=https://ncph.org/history-at-work/ironbound-ej-history/|access-date=2021-12-16|language=en-US|archive-date=December 16, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211216225159/https://ncph.org/history-at-work/ironbound-ej-history/|url-status=live}} for being a leader in [[environmental justice]] led by a local [[community organizing]] and advocacy organization called the Ironbound Community Corporation (ICC) and an offshoot group the Ironbound Committee Against Toxic Waste (ICATW). ICC and ICATW have worked over the years with other local and national groups and figures such as [[Greenpeace]], [[Lois Gibbs]], and the Newark Coalition for Neighborhoods.{{Cite web|last=picturingjustice|title=By Actor (Group or Individual) - Picturing Justice|url=https://picturingjustice.tumblr.com/actor|access-date=2021-12-16|website=By Actor (Group or Individual) Group: • Coalition to Save Rent Control • Elizabeth Coalition to House the Homeless • Grassroots Environmental Organization • Greater Newark Bay Coalition •...}} Over the years they have worked on a number of environmental justice issues including airplane noise, dioxin, pollution and fumes.{{Cite web|title=History of ICC|url=https://www.ejintheironbound.com/historyicc|access-date=2021-12-16|website=Environmental Justice in The Ironbound|language=en-US|archive-date=December 16, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211216225157/https://www.ejintheironbound.com/historyicc|url-status=live}}{{Cite news|last=picturingjustice|title=Photos By Struggle - Picturing Justice|url=https://picturingjustice.tumblr.com/struggle|access-date=2021-12-16|newspaper=Tumblr|archive-date=December 16, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211216225158/https://picturingjustice.tumblr.com/struggle|url-status=live}} In 1983, dangerous levels of [[Polychlorinated dibenzodioxins|dioxin]] were discovered at an abandoned chemical factory in the Ironbound.{{Cite news|last=Sullivan|first=Joseph F.|title=Company Settles Lawsuit Over Exposure to Dioxin|work=The New York Times Company|date=25 January 1992|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1992/01/25/nyregion/company-settles-lawsuit-over-exposure-to-dioxin.html|archive-date=January 16, 2018|access-date=November 6, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180116013926/http://www.nytimes.com/1992/01/25/nyregion/company-settles-lawsuit-over-exposure-to-dioxin.html|url-status=live}} The [[Diamond Alkali]] Company was largely responsible for this pollution through their heavy production of [[Agent Orange]] between 1951 and 1969. The off-site cleanup was completed by 1986, and in 1989 the site received a permanent impermeable cap. In the 1980s residents protested against a [[garbage incinerator]] in the neighborhood. The incinerator was built in 1990 but residents have continued to protest environmental issues over the years. Bright pink and purple fumes were often seen spewing from the facility but [[Covanta]], the company operating the incinerator, blamed a local hospital for improperly disposed medical waste. In summer 2019, ICC partnered with [[Earthjustice]], a nonprofit [[public interest]] organization that [[litigation|litigates]] to [[environmental protection|protect the environment]], and the Environmental Advocacy Clinic at [[Vermont Law School]] urged state officials to investigate. Covanta has been found many hundreds of times to exceed air pollution limits or to fail to abide by required safety regulations. Covanta eventually acknowledged that the fumes were produced by its burning of [[pesticide]]s improperly disposed and agreed to new waste management procedures.Earthjustice, 22 Jan. 2021 [https://earthjustice.org/features/ironbound-unyielding "A Newark Neighborhood Takes on a Toxic Trash Incinerator"]
